recommendation.interactive: Keep batch16, prepare1, publish1 and existing 384/448MiB application budgets. Best conservative tested profile, but backlog latency remains an open limitation.
recommendation.bulk: Opt-in batch64, prepare1, publish2 for ingest/reindex without interactive latency priority; repeated B results below, not the isolated P2B.2 throughput.

limits: One ZIP; no claim about all AO3 dumps or SQLite import paths.
Shared host, warm OS page cache and uncontrolled merge/JIT variation; no exclusive attribution of all speedup to concurrency.

Complete-source hashes compared to P2A authoritative legacy builder on same identities/timestamps; P2A had previously matched P1B.1. Independent fresh ingests legitimately have different UUID/date fields.

Cold C clones retain same IDs and initial segments; schema039 is held constant while comparing legacy runtime. Backlog work drained differs substantially; latency is not a matched number of indexed documents per second.
Event-loop diagnostics use bins whose end falls in probe window; boundary bin overlap and sampling resolution prevent exact attribution.
Container working set is not RSS. PostgreSQL shared RSS is not summed across backend processes; per-container sampled cgroup memory and Node process RSS are provided.
Header-level profiler HTTP and runtime HTTP-through-response-parsing durations differ; use bulk.http_ms for full-text service time.

Initial preload emitted preparation-input counters only on process exit; SIGTERM in B did not flush those optional counters. A captures all inputs and final B2 repeat flushes deltas per durable pass. Missing counters are not interpreted as zero. Runtime route and zero legacy SQL/PUT are checked independently.
Empty-queue samples are the 30 seconds following API readiness and can include JIT/background initialization, not an indefinitely warmed steady state.
No synthetic rate cap, disabling of durability, cache rewrite, new worker or further architecture was used to mask latency regression.

bottleneck.assessment: Canonical ingest finishes much earlier than projections. Current/historical catalog under shared API CPU and SQL contention supplies the critical path; B1 can retain a short text tail. B2 publishers are often underfilled. This is not evidence of whole-host or solely OpenSearch saturation.
bottleneck.next_step: Profile catalog service versus SQL waiting and shared API event-loop occupancy, then design execution isolation in a separately authorized phase. No ZIP parallelism or canonical rewrite justified as the immediate cure by these runs.

runtime_change.mechanism: Cooperative setImmediate after >=8ms between HTML extraction tasks and between document encodings; no sleep, rate cap, new lane or serializer change
runtime_change.limitation: One synchronous task may exceed the slice; shared SQL/OpenSearch contention remains

comparison_notes: Historical P0 includes 6128 extra projections; later runs do not.
P0/P1A comparable backlog P95 absent; use null rather than invent a comparison.
Historical P1B.1 backlog P95 166.21ms is shown separately from the contemporary same-clone controls.
Operational B2 changes both batch and publishing concurrency; it is not a one-factor concurrency ablation.
